subject: Urgent: Suncrest live-stream degradations — routing and TCP keepalive hypothesis
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@suncresthealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@suncresthealth.com>, engops@suncresthealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Live demo feed dropping / long pauses (region: us-east-1)

Hi Kimberly,

We started a product demo for clinicians this morning and saw repeated long pauses in the live transcription feed — each pause lasts ~8-12s of silence, then the stream catches up with a burst. It looks like token streaming stalls rather than complete disconnects. This hit two demo rooms concurrently (room-402 & room-813).

Symptoms:
- WebSocket stays open, but no chunked events for 8–12s.
- Client eventually receives resumed chunks with many tokens at once.
- No explicit 5xx errors visible on our side.

This is blocking our pilot launch next week. Can you please advise next steps and what logs you need? I attached a screenshot we captured.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
Senior PM, Clinical Apps
Suncrest Health

Attachments: screenshot-ws-frames-12feb.png

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@suncresthealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@suncresthealth.com>, engops@suncresthealth.com, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Live demo feed dropping / long pauses (region: us-east-1)

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. Sorry you're seeing this during a demo.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you share a HAR or client-side WebSocket capture for one of the affected sessions (room-402 if possible)?
2) If you can, turn on debug logging on your client for streaming frames (we'll take any timestamps).

Connor — looping you in to triage. Initial hypothesis from support: sustained token backlog + keepalive mismatch on the proxy path causing chunk buffering, then burst delivery. Please prioritize.

I'll keep Suncrest updated and escalate if we confirm the issue is on our egress path.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@suncresthealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@suncresthealth.com>, engops@suncresthealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Live demo feed dropping / long pauses (region: us-east-1)

On Fri, Feb 12, 2027 at 09:42 AM kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Connor — looping you in to triage. Initial hypothesis from support: sustained token backlog + keepalive mismatch on the proxy path causing chunk buffering, then burst delivery. Please prioritize.

Thanks Kimberly, Liam — I'm investigating now. Quick summary of what I'm collecting:
- Ingress logs (proxy/frontend) for the timeframe 09:00–09:30 ET
- Serving runtime metrics (per-request delay, kv-cache pressure, batching statistics)
- Egress TCP keepalive and chunked transfer size distribution

Preliminary observations (09:06–09:22):
- Several requests show steady token generation but delayed flushes at the proxy (proxy flush intervals spiking to 8–12s)
- CPU on the model pods is normal; batching isn't saturating GPUs.
- There are short-lived network retransmits between front proxy and the streaming layer, coincident with flush gaps.

Hypothesis: a middlebox (customer proxy or a shared infra hop) is coalescing small chunked frames due to TCP Nagle-like buffering or mismatched keepalive/idle timeouts, causing the WebSocket client to see silence then a burst.

Immediate mitigations I'm trying:
- Force explicit chunk-flush on the proxy layer for affected routes for next 30 minutes.
- Enable more aggressive streaming-heartbeat (send empty chunk every 1s) for the trial account.

I'll attach logs once sanitized.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: harvest-logs-2027-02-12.txt

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@suncresthealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@suncresthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 13:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Live demo feed dropping / long pauses (region: us-east-1)

Thanks for the quick action. Additional detail from EngOps:
- We run a client-side edge proxy (managed by our network team) between clinician devices and our cloud services.
- The proxy has a 10s idle-coalescing window for small TCP writes, which we recently deployed to reduce connection churn.

If Connor's hypothesis is correct, this change would explain the 8–12s gaps. We can rollback the edge proxy change immediately if Redwood confirms that explicit flush will help while we evaluate a permanent config change.

— Priya
Priya Shah
Director, Engineering Operations
Suncrest Health

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@suncresthealth.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@suncresthealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:11:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Live demo feed dropping / long pauses (region: us-east-1)

Hi all — follow-up after the weekend tests.

What we did:
- Enabled immediate chunk flush on the proxy for Suncrest's routing key (experiment window: 09:00–11:00 ET).
- Deployed short heartbeat frames from runtime every 1s for streaming sessions tied to the trial account.

Result:
- No observed 8–12s silent gaps during the test window. Client-side captures show steady token-level arrival.
- We still see occasional micro-retransmits on the path, but those don't cause multi-second silence once flushes are enforced.

Recommendation:
- Suncrest should rollback the 10s coalescing change on their edge proxy or exempt traffic to Redwood streaming endpoints.
- We will ship a default defensive flush configuration for trial/demos and add a per-account toggle in Console within two weeks.

For visibility and exec context: Kimberly, I copied Sean given this is a pilot launch and may require commercial accommodations should Suncrest need rollback assistance.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@suncresthealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@suncresthealth.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Live demo feed dropping / long pauses (region: us-east-1)

Liam/Priya — great to hear the experiment validated the hypothesis. Thank you for toggling the edge change promptly.

Next steps:
- Suncrest: please confirm when you've toggled the proxy exemption. If you'd like, Redwood can coordinate a small rollback window with your network team — we can provide an engineer on the call.
- Redwood: we'll fast-track a per-account streaming-flush toggle and add documentation to the runbook. Connor will own the engineering task; I'll own the customer comms.
- Commercial: If this rollback impacts your launch timeline materially and you need a goodwill concession, let me know and I'll escalate.

Sean — for awareness: this surfaced during a paid pilot and caused a demo failure. There may be asks for credits or extended trial. If you want to weigh in on a standard approach (one-time credit for pilot-impacting infra/ops issues), please advise and I'll action.

Thanks —
— Kimberly
